title: Cancer: current or history, and metastases
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cancer as documented at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for liver metastases.

HPI
Pt is an 80-year-old male with a history of colon cancer. Primary tumor was surgically removed and treated several years ago. Pt reports feeling well currently. Previous imaging showed no evidence of local recurrence at the primary site. However, pt presents today for management of metastatic to the liver. Pt denies new abdominal pain, weight loss, or jaundice.

Medication List
Lisinopril 10mg daily
Atorvastatin 20mg daily

Exam
Gen: Well-appearing, alert, oriented x3.
Vitals: BP 132/80, HR 72, RR 16, Temp 98.6F, SpO2 98% on RA.
Abd: Soft, non-tender, non-distended. Normal bowel sounds.
CV: RRR, CTAB.
Resp: CTAB.
Ext: WNL.

Assessment
1. Liver metastases from prior colon carcinoma.
2. History of colon cancer, stable.

Plan
1. Continue monitoring of liver metastasis.
2. Discussed supportive care and symptom management.
3. F/u in 3 months for repeat imaging.

Electronically signed, K. Nguyen, MD, 05/12/2026
explanations: The colon cancer was excised or eradicated, no treatment is directed to it and there is no evidence of it: personal history Z85.038 (no HCC). Any metastasis is still coded as a current secondary malignancy.
Liver metastases: C78.7, secondary malignant neoplasm of liver (HCC 17).

distractors.why: Treatment ended and there is no evidence of the primary: code personal history (Z85), not active cancer.
Metastasis is coded as a secondary malignancy, even when the primary is history.
The metastases are in the liver, not bone.

hccs.label: Cancer Metastatic to Lung/Liver/Brain/and Other Organs; Acute Myeloid Leukemia Except Promyelocytic
